# Lab 7 — Taking the unsafe code out of a ring buffer

**Unit:** [week 7, memory safety III: regions, unsafe code and its tools](../../week07-regions-unsafe.md)
(exercises 2–3). **Time:** 2 hours. **Runs in the playground:** no

The playground's older compiler runs the solution but prints a wrong total
for the region part (99 instead of 124), so check this lab with `fid`.

The week's ring buffer manages eight words of memory by hand behind
`unsafe` blocks. You replace the raw block by a `Vec`, remove every
`unsafe`, and use the ring inside a region that frees each frame's memory
in one step.

## Start

- [Open the starter in the playground](https://fides-lang.org/playground#) to read it, and
- copy [`starter.fd`](starter.fd): `fid run starter.fd` prints the sum of
  the last eight values.

Embed:

```html
<iframe src="https://fides-lang.org/playground/embed.html#"
        width="100%" height="420" style="border:0" title="Lab 7 starter"></iframe>
```

## Tasks

1. **No more unsafe.** Replace `base: i64` by `slots: Vec<i64>`, created
   with eight zeros by `ring_new`; use `get` and `set`. Remove every
   `unsafe` block, `p_malloc` and `p_free` (and `ring_free`: who frees the
   buffer now?). The sum must not change. `fid audit starter.fd` lists the
   unsafe sites a program reaches: compare before and after.
2. **Items.** Write `ring_items(r: &Ring) -> str`, the values from oldest
   to newest separated by spaces, and print it after the sum as
   `oldest to newest: ...`.
3. **A region per frame.** For three frames, create a ring inside
   `region scratch { ... }`, push `(frame * 7 + i) % 13` for `i` in
   `0..20`, and add its sum to a total declared outside the region. Print
   `three frames total <n>`.

## Check your work

When you are done, `fid run starter.fd` prints:

```text
last 8 sum to 52
oldest to newest: 3 4 5 6 7 8 9 10
three frames total 124
```

## Questions to hand in

- `fid explain starter.fd ring_sum`: is the bounds check of
  `r.slots.get((r.head + i) % 8)` kept or removed, and why?
- The total is declared outside the region and assigned inside it. Why is
  that allowed for an `i64` and not for a `Vec` the region pushes to
  (proposal 0005)?
